root_cause: The scheduled recovery controller could call an undefined BRAIN dispatcher, fail to reliably recognize exact-head in-flight Required runs, and stop revisiting merged nonterminal obligations after 24 hours; repeated closure attempts could amplify provider load rather than converge. The first protected merge also exposed a pre-existing gap: the canonical learning path-validation gate only ran after merging, permitting a non-brain test path to enter main.
prevention: Never add a competing Github scheduler when the existing canonical recovery supervisor can be hardened.
Recovery-run identity must bind the PR number and immutable candidate SHA and avoid dispatch when that logical flight is already active.
The supervisor must never invoke an undefined BRAIN dispatch path or assume a recovery happened on a skipped invocation.
Nonterminal merged obligations remain auditable and bounded by a seven-day check horizon, 90-minute retry cooldown and three-attempt limit.
Only canonical post-merge production readback plus durable authority evidence can mark an obligation LIVE_BEWEZEN.
The canonical Brain learning evaluation gate must run in Required preflight before protected merge and reject missing/non-Brain test paths.
Quote the canonical terminal closure workflow run-name; unquoted # starts a YAML comment and loses the PR number, breaking exact-PR deduplication.
Terminal closure must check the real .github/workflows/codeql.yml workflow; fail regression on any reference to a nonexistent powerhouse-codeql.yml.
When Required test adds a new preflight artifact, rebuild stale candidates from current main instead of copying runtime proof artifacts into outdated branches.

success_criteria: Exact-head Required + CodeQL pass without duplicate dispatch
Production Readback and durable canonical obligation terminal evidence succeed before any LIVE_BEWEZEN claim
